relationship_to_restored_text: Interpretive contemplative layer aligned by verse. This does not replace the source-audited restored translation.

verses.mystical_translation: Nahash dies, and Hanun inherits a throne inside grief.
David sends comforters to honor an old bond.
Hanun's advisers reinterpret consolation as espionage.
Fear becomes sexualized public humiliation of messengers.
The injured men receive privacy at Jericho until they are ready to return.
Anticipating retaliation, Ammon spends immense silver to buy military support.
Hired forces and local cities assemble around Medeba.
David answers with Joab and the royal army.
Ammon defends the city while allied kings hold the field.
Joab divides the army against threats on two fronts.
Abishai receives responsibility for the Ammonite line.
The brothers promise mutual rescue rather than solitary heroism.
Courage is invoked for people and cities, while outcome is left to YHWH.
The Aramean force flees Joab's advance.
Ammon retreats into the city, and the first campaign pauses.
Aram gathers a larger transriver force under Shophach.
David mobilizes all Israel and crosses the Jordan.
Tens of thousands die, and Shophach is killed.
Defeated allies accept service under David and abandon Ammon.

contemplative_note: A funeral visit becomes war because suspicion answers vulnerability with humiliation. The story's constructive moments are small: giving shamed people privacy, and brothers promising to rescue one another. The destructive momentum is enormous: fear, money, mobilization, mass death, and peace reduced to submission.
